framework: Classical Sanskrit metres with syllable counts, gana patterns, and example verses

anushtubh.name: Anushtubh
anushtubh.notes: Most common metre in Vedas and epics; also called Ashtaka
anushtubh.example: agnI medhA jushA RM mayA mat_tam upA gam
anushtubh.example_slp1: agnI medhA jushA RM mayA mat_tam upA gam

trishtubh.name: Trishtubh
trishtubh.notes: Verse metre with 11 syllables per quarter; complex internal structure

jagati.name: Jagati
jagati.notes: Extended verse metre; 12 syllables per quarter; used in Vedic chanting

vasantatilaka.name: Vasantatilaka
vasantatilaka.notes: Half-similar metres; used in classical Sanskrit kavya; 14 syllables per pada

mandakranta.name: Mandakranta
mandakranta.notes: Dissimilar metre with 17 syllables; complex structure; prized in kavya literature

shardula-vikridita.name: Shardula-Vikridita
shardula-vikridita.notes: Verse metre used in classical poetry; 19 syllables; subtle rhythmic pattern

nata-navaraja.name: Nata-Navaraja
nata-navaraja.notes: Metres used in dramatic/ verse; 16 syllables per pada

metre_categories.sama: Metres with identical pattern in all four quarters (padas)
metre_categories.ardhasama: Metres where first two and last two quarters have same pattern
metre_categories.vishama: Metres with all different patterns in each quarter

matching_rules.partial_match: Submetre pattern matches; may be incomplete verse
matching_rules.unknown: No significant match found with known metres

confidence_scoring.calculation: Levenshtein distance normalized by pattern length
